subject: inla.posterior.samples() hanging without an error on Google Cloud

messages.author: 5f8ff981212931fb
messages.subject: inla.posterior.samples() hanging without an error on Google Cloud
parts:
Hi,

 When I run inla.posterior.samples() on my laptop (macOS 10.15.4, R version 3.6.0, and the latest stable INLA download, which I believe is 20.3.17), it runs with no issues (see 'laptop_run.png'). When I run it on a Google Cloud machine running rocker/verse:3.6.0, the code hangs with no error on the inla_qsample step (see 'gcloud_run.png'). My code is below. I saw a post stating that inla.dynload.workaround() is deprecated and I should use inla.binary.install() instead, but inla.binary.install() requires interactive user input that I cannot provide as I am trying to run this code in a remote session. 

Any advice much appreciated,
Amelia

code, where nsamp=1, inla_outputs is a list of outputs from different regressions, and to_extract_vals is a character vector: 

    print("Extracting posterior draws")
    model_out <- inla_outputs[[1]][["model_output"]]
    
    to_extract_names <- c(rownames(model_out$summary.fixed), "field")
    to_extract_vals <- as.list(rep(0, length(to_extract_names)))
    names(to_extract_vals) <- to_extract_names
    
    print(paste("Finding", nsamp, "raw posterior samples"))
    INLA:::inla.dynload.workaround()
    tic <- Sys.time()
    raw_samples <- inla.posterior.sample(nsamp, model_out, selection = to_extract_vals, verbose = T)
    toc <- Sys.time()
    print("Raw posterior samples found!")
    elapsed <- toc-tic
    print(paste("--> Time Elapsed: ", elapsed, units(elapsed)))

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] inla.posterior.samples() hanging without an error on Google Cloud
parts:
I have not seen this before. Not anyone that running on a G Cloud machine as well.

Two things comes to mind. 

I guess you have verified that it runs at all, like that

inla(y~1,data=data.frame(y=0))

Returns something that is not an error. 

Next, is something with parallelism. Can you check if its run when you set

inla.setOption(num.threads=1)

Or 2, 4, etc. By default, it uses as many it can. Maybe there is something there. 

Let me know. 

H

-- 
Håvard Rue 
Helpdesk 
he...@r-inla.org

parts:
Thanks for the feedback.

Two more things.

- Can you upgrade to the most recent testing version?
inla.upgrade(testing=TRUE)

- If that does not help, can you try to set option skew.corr=FALSE,
like

inla.posterior.sample(..., skew.corr=FALSE)

and check if that makes any difference?

let me know.

thx
H
